meta.description: Analyzes single-cell pooled CRISPR screens across RNA, protein, and chromatin readouts.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: Synthetic results are labeled and no citations or statistics were invented.

practice_boundaries.detail: The shipped Scope section supported the patient-treatment refusal.

methodological_ground.detail: Planted-effect and budget checks support the documented analysis paths.

code_usability.detail: All Python files compile; working paths execute. SCEPTRE produces valid tables but its post-computation exit-139 instability is a P1 runtime defect, not a syntax/dependency absence.

functional_suitability.note: Broad coverage is present; the advertised full Pertpy route was not bounded in fresh execution.

reliability.note: Mixscape and assignment are deterministic; both shipped SCEPTRE paths end with a segmentation fault.

performance_context.note: References/scripts are well split, but the full example exceeded 22 GB before output.

agent_usability.note: Clear workflow, thresholds, and current API guidance.

human_usability.note: Natural prompts and decision rules are clear; unexecutable optional paths remain.

security.note: No secrets or raw-string execution; ordinary file paths are not validated.

maintainability.note: Runnable blocks are split and compile, but two runtime regressions require environment-level diagnosis.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger, references, scope boundary, and reproducibility guidance.

recommendations.title: Stabilize SCEPTRE runtime exit
recommendations.problem: Both shipped SCEPTRE paths write valid result tables but then exit 139 after computation.
recommendations.root_cause: The R/sceptre native runtime tears down unreliably in this audited environment; the script has no containment or known-good execution route.
recommendations.fix: Reproduce and isolate the native crash with the pinned R/sceptre stack, then document a known-good environment or wrapper that exits 0; re-run both shipped branches.

recommendations.title: Bound the full Pertpy example
recommendations.problem: The copied real Papalexi example passed 22 GB RSS without producing its promised TSV and had to be stopped.
recommendations.root_cause: It loads and processes the full dataset in one unbounded process.
recommendations.fix: Provide a parameterized subset/smoke mode and memory estimate, or refactor the full example to a bounded workflow before claiming it as a generally runnable example.

recommendations.title: State executable limits for optional methods
recommendations.problem: FR-Perturb is not installable in this Python-3.12 environment and Seurat is absent.
recommendations.root_cause: The references name alternatives without a verified local execution route.
recommendations.fix: Add a supported environment recipe or an explicit unavailable-here note with a tested fallback.
